ideas.title: Glassblowing at a beach furnace
ideas.critique: This round fixes what was weak in round 2. A full 3D discrete viscous shell with per-vertex thickness and temperature, a viscosity that follows VFT and a rotating frame means a crooked piece really is crooked, and glowing to clear refracting glass shows off the tracer from start to finish. The risk is size: a GPU viscous-shell solver is several sessions of work, and if it gets simplified into an inflating balloon with a colour ramp it becomes the morphing mesh the pitch promises to avoid. A furnace place with a shelf is the predictable part.

ideas.title: Ants: draw a honey trail, then they take over
ideas.critique: Stigmergy now drives cooperative rigid-body transport. Summed pulls that turn and stall the biscuit are emergent and can be read, and drawing the road gives the player a real verb instead of watching. Pale crumbs and a head-sized biscuit answer the specks-on-grass worry. The pig-bed joke is the obvious gag, though, and the race against friends eating the biscuit will be scripted unless the eating is itself simulated.

ideas.title: Swing on vines through the pine wood
ideas.critique: Grappling and swinging is one of the most familiar movement mechanics in games, so it surprises less than the other two ideas. A verlet rope, a massed body and a ballistic release are a correct but modest pendulum setup. It is still the strongest play loop of the round, with momentum skill people would replay, and it reuses the climbing ray work for something you can see. A small island wood with few branches may make the chains of swings short and samey.
